title: Owner runs W-001 over whole C:\ to discharge SL-089 criterion 3
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. A person has run W-001 over the whole of C:\ unelevated, from pwsh as `-Root C:\`, with the wcifs-layer-store precaution on, and the run wrote .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json (scope whole-drive, elevated false, checkerElevated false, checkerControls all true, verdict held): missing
2. In c-drive-run.json the panel's rows equal the engine's failed-folder count: rows = header = coreUnreadable: missing
3. No refused-then-listed folder is a row (oracle.openRefusedButOpenable 0, no console 'LEAK:' line), while about 306,000 such folders exist on C:\: missing
4. No row has an empty reason, and no folder is a row twice (emptyReasons 0, duplicates 0): missing

5. The whole-drive counts are near the expected values: about 682–684 rows (≈652 code 5, ≈28 code 363, ≈2 code 1920); about 30 leftover rows (oracle.leftoverRows code363 + reparse); verdict held; duplicates 0 (SC-136/SC-138 expectations folded in): missing

Criterion 5 asks for about 682-684 rows (652/28/2), but those counts were measured with the container layer store scanned. The run the slice requires leaves the store out, and Test-W001 fails a whole-drive run that does not. Does the person accept criterion 5 as met when the record's counts are explained item by item: rows at most about 660, code 363 27-28, code 1920 0-2, notScanned 1, every difference from 682 named? The only like-for-like alternative is a scan with the precaution off, which brings back the wcifs.sys pool growth.
Uncontested; one proposal. Where the criterion-5 reconciliation table lives (the new SL-107 doc, or appended to SL-089-seams.md) is a placement choice the reviewer may reverse.

Uncontested; one proposal. Teeing the console into artifacts\ versus asking the person to keep the window's scrollback is a convenience choice. The design picks Tee-Object because the hook log is deleted.
The whole-C:\ W-001 run and the record .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json: the person's run (SC-136, SC-138). Nothing was run on whole C:\, and no engine stage may.

Cases C-009 to C-013 (timeout, elevated shell, precaution off, app stopped mid-scan, -Root C: without backslash, committed file holding a path): marked not material in the design and needing a click, an elevated session, a 20-minute run or a code change. Their code paths are read in the doc; the committed-path case is covered by the rule and its corpus.
Exposing the refused-then-listed count in the schema-1 report (Core and report change, scanner tier): filed for later in the design.

Raising the 1,200 s wait in Test-W001 or editing the guard comment at WindowCases.ps1 lines 6199-6200: not needed, and any edit to that file makes WindowMutants -Mutant All a required validate check (Q-114).
Any edit to .taad/slices/SL-089/index.json: an export of the engine store (Q-106).
An architecture-record edit: no block's sentence became untrue.
Once the person's record is committed, the awaiting_file entry in plants.json can be dropped (the rule then matches a real file); keeping it is harmless.
The harness's awaiting_file allowance has no RuleCases case of its own: it is covered by C-007 and by a manual negative run (listed file present but unmatched exits 2). A RuleCases case would pin it.
If the person's run ends TIMEOUT, raise the 1,200 literal in Invoke-HookedRun 'rows' inside Test-W001 (then run WindowMutants -Mutant All per Q-114).
Expose the refused-then-listed count (LastAccessAsked minus Kept minus Unreadable.Count, per U-102) in the report so a W-001 record can show the roughly 306,000 context figure.
Reconcile the per-run pool guard figure (0.5 GB in older docs, 3 GB in the engine's watch) in lesson #357 and SL-089-seams.md when convenient; this slice depends on neither.

deviation: The design said change no code. The engine-appended counts-only rule matches no file until the person commits the record, and the repo's harness (eng/rules-harness/harness.py) refuses a clean baseline with an unmatched rule: it exited 2 on this tree, and RuleCases C-007 and Q-027's validate run would fail with it. I added a small allowance, awaiting_file in plants.json, read by load_awaiting and check_clean. A listed rule may match nothing only while its file is absent from the scratch copy. Both ends were checked: present-but-unmatched still blocks (exit 2), and unlisted-unmatched still blocks. RuleCases -Case All passed.

deviation: m1's literal fix ('\\\\|/') was widened to a closed grammar (any slash, any backslash that is not a JSON quote or code-unit escape, the u005c/u002f spellings). Reason: a path typed with single backslashes (C:\temp\new) is valid JSON and the pair pattern misses it; the corpus shows it. This is what the CLOSE THE CLASS obligation asks for.

deviation: The rule's engine check (m2) was built as harness plant rows (S83-S86, P36) rather than as a validate-time scratch step, and the design's 'add no code/tests' became two runnable scripts in tests/bugs. The owed cases C-001 to C-006 need commands the engine can run; a doc check alone feeds no shape.

deviation: The design record .taad/slices/SL-107/design-slice-1.json was edited as the builder instruction required (patterns, would_force_resynthesis). It is an engine export and may be overwritten on refresh (Q-106).

deviation: No workaround, setting or notice was added: the run depends on the existing wcifs-layer-store entry (outside defect in wcifs.sys). Both positions of its switch and the on-screen notice are covered by the existing cases, which I ran: X-004 (store left out, 'not scanned', the notice beside the totals) and X-005 (off through the confirmation, on again next launch).
